title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
read_level: full main text (pdftotext of v1); appendices skimmed (compute, protocol)
why_wsp: Five LLM agents edit trained vision classifiers' weights through a sandbox tool interface (WeightLab) without gradients to relabel concepts or fix errors; the paper also proposes Edit-Ready Training that rehearses the closed-form edits these LLMs make so networks become easier to edit.
domain: image classification editing (Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS, Entity-30)
editor: GPT-6 Astra (high effort), Claude Opus 5.5 (default effort), GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Gemma-4-26B
target: ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-B/16 classifiers (ImageNet-initialized, fine-tuned); head up to 61,470 parameters (ResNet-50 on Entity-30)
interface: code/tensor tools (WeightLab: inspect predictions/activations/weights, set/add/scale entries, rows, channels, tensors; undo/reset)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (up to 20 forward probes, 30 weight reads, 8 edit calls per edit process)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "The median edit process takes about three minutes for Astra and Opus, with a median of 252 and 27 changed weights." (Appendix H); Opus head edits touch "median 11 to 64 feature columns, 2–8% of the features" (Sec 5.3)

headline_results.claim: ERT has highest mean net score for both main editors
headline_results.quote: ERT has the highest mean net score for both editors (Astra: 0.74, against 0.71 for ENN, 0.63 for LS and 0.63 for ERM; Opus: 0.72, against 0.68, 0.65 and 0.60).
ERT's gain over ERM is +0.12 for both (p < 0.001 over the paired edit processes)
ERT is ahead of ENN by +0.03 (Astra) and +0.04 (Opus) on average, which is not significant (p = 0.10 and p = 0.07).
On the Entity-30 confusion fix it raises the net score from 0.46 to 0.79 for Astra and from 0.44 to 0.74 for Opus
For all training methods, accuracy on the full test sets still ends 3 to 4 points below the unedited network after the final edit.

headline_results.claim: Opus edits are rank-one head edits along support/reference contrast
headline_results.quote: in 69 of its 73 edit processes on ERM-trained networks Opus edits the head, with a rank-one change along the contrast between support and reference images
GLM-5.3-Flash and Gemma-4-26B are much weaker (0.45 and 0.30, against 0.68 for Opus)

headline_results.claim: Edit budget beyond 8 calls does not help
headline_results.quote: Against 8 calls in the same pilot, neither 4 nor 12 calls change the net score detectably

cost.quote: The median edit process takes about three minutes for Astra and Opus
The three open-weight editors consumed about 750 million prompt tokens.
we trained about 1,300 networks. Training them ... took about 385 GPU-hours

baselines_and_controls: network training methods ERM, label smoothing, Editable Neural Networks (ENN), ERT; five editors under identical protocol and blinding; seed ablation; edit-rule, backbone-edit and edit-budget ablations; comparison of LLM edits to closed-form edits (cosine similarity)
runs_and_variance: eight edit requests per editor/setting/method; 292 Astra, 308 Opus, 757 open-weight scored edit processes in main grid; >2,600 total; 95% bootstrap CIs and paired sign-flip tests; "variation between networks ... standard deviation of 0.00 (95% CI upper bound 0.03), whereas edit processes on the same network vary by 0.17" (Sec 5.2)
robustness_of_edits: scored on held-out test images for success and side effects; sequences of edits and robustness to fine-tuning not tested
verification: statistical (held-out evaluation, bootstrap CIs, sign-flip tests); none formal
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a; LLM edits closely resemble a closed-form rank-one re-route along the feature contrast (mean cosine 0.72 to 0.93 on eight of nine settings)
limitations_stated: Only image classification, three backbones, four datasets; 8 to 16 paired edit processes per cell so only large differences detectable; hyperparameters tuned with scripted editors on ResNet-18; edits still lower test accuracy.
code_or_data: project page https://viscom.uni-ulm.de/wsp; framework, tasks, trajectories and scores "will be released"
cites_or_builds_on: Editable Neural Networks, Sinitsin et al. (ref [36])
notes_for_survey: Flips the WSP question to the target side: trains networks to be easier for LLM editors, using closed-form rules distilled from observed Opus edits. Also a multi-editor vision benchmark with side-effect scoring; finds LLM edits are mostly sparse rank-one head edits, close to a closed-form rule.
